title: Backward Compatibility in Tree-Based Explanations and Enhanced CART Algorithm

problem.claim: Model updates can change explanations and thereby harm downstream decision-making for users of explainable models, including decision-tree explanations.

gap.claim: Existing research has focused on feature-contribution explanations and does not handle explanations derived from tree structures.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Backward Compatibility Loss in Tree-based eXplanations (BCLTX), a loss metric intended to suppress changes in decision-tree explanations before and after model updates.
The paper introduces CART with Backward Compatibility in Tree-based eXplanations (CART-BCTX), a lightweight algorithm that improves upon CART for decision-tree updates under BCLTX.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on 10 real-world datasets covering classification and regression tasks report favorable trade-offs between prediction performance and BCLTX values for CART-BCTX.
The authors report computation times for CART-BCTX comparable to CART across the evaluated tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Model updates are fundamental but can affect downstream decision-making.
Changes in explanations after updates can harm users, with decision trees providing a prominent risk-sensitive example.
Prior work does not address explanations derived from tree structures.
The paper proposes BCLTX and develops CART-BCTX for tree updates under that loss.
Experiments across 10 real-world classification and regression datasets report performance, compatibility, and computation-time results.

source_observation.claim: Model updates can change explanations in ways that negatively affect users.

interpretation.claim: Update quality for explainable models should account for explanation stability in addition to predictive performance.

application.claim: When updating tree-based models, evaluate a compatibility objective such as BCLTX alongside prediction performance.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify whether this trade-off applies beyond the reported 10 real-world datasets or to explanation settings other than tree structures.

unknowns: The abstract does not define how BCLTX is computed.
The abstract does not describe the datasets, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not specify the update scenarios or evaluation protocol.
